newsitem.title: POLAND: Analysts see consolidation among Polish brokerages.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see consolidation among Polish brokerages.

text.p: The current consolidation wave of Polish banks should be accompanied by consolidation among securities houses, analysts said at a conference on Wednesday marking the fifth anniversary of BRE brokerage.
One banking group already formed around state-owned Bank Pekao SA and another between BIG and Bank Gdanski have said their brokerage activities would merge.

Analysts said the envisioned group currently forming around BPH, PBR, Kredyt Bank, insurer Warta and state-owned Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) should lead to the consolidation of their brokerages.

"I think in two to three years the number of brokerages could shrink to between 10 and 20 from the current 50," Piotr Kowalczewski, board member of BIG SA brokerage, told Reuters after the conference.
Kowalczewski said smaller brokerages without a foreign partner or niche specialisation, or not wealthy enough to provide a full range of services, would face extinction.
Tomasz Mazurczak, investment adviser at BRE brokers, said smaller brokerages might choose to pursue discount brokering.

The head of the Polish Securities Commission, Jacek Socha, said the role of Polish brokerage houses was more important than their number, which could remain the same as more brokerages form while others die.

"There are currently 50 brokerages but most are small with only a few thousand accounts," Socha told Reuters, adding that the number of large active brokerages, with or without foreign partners, would remain at around 10.
